messages:
maria: quick follow-up to the kernel-autotune RFC -- we need a concrete policy for prioritizing probe budgets across tenants. current approach is first-come-first-served and it's causing noisy neighbors during morning spike. thoughts?
kevin: agree. saw tenant A consume ~70% of probe tokens for 20m this morning, starving smaller tenants. quick data:
kevin: `tenant,probes,avg_latency_ms`
kevin: `A,4200,18.7`
kevin: `B,600,31.2`
kevin: `C,200,29.1`
jia: can we weight probes by recent traffic + SLA tier? e.g. budget = base + alpha * recent_qps + beta * sla_weight. keeps small tenants from being zeroed.
sam: SLA weight makes sense but watch for latency cliffs when we throttle probes; some kernels only reveal efficiency after many probes. we should stagger probing to avoid simultaneous cold-to-hot transitions.
olivia: proposal: a 3-level prioritization queue: reserved (enterprise contracts), proportional (by qps smoothing), and opportunistic (best-effort). enforce per-node caps so one tenant can't saturate a single GPU's probe window. dashboard needs to show probe consumption by tenant + rolling 1h heatmap.
dmitri: also consider probe value estimation: not all probes are equally informative. compute expected_speedup = (latency_current - latency_estimated_with_new_kernel) * traffic_weight, and prioritize probes with higher expected_speedup. we can approximate with model of kernel performance per seq-len bucket.
maria: good point. how do we get that estimate cheap? running full microbench per variant is expensive.
kevin: cheap heuristics: sample 5-10 traces per seq-len bucket, run them through candidate kernels with shortened seq or reduced batch to get a delta estimate. cost ~5-10 probes per bucket instead of full sweep. example script we ran:
kevin: ```
kevin: # probe-sampled.sh
kevin: for seq in 32 64 128 256; do
kevin:   tail -n +1 traces_${seq}.json | shuf -n 8 | xargs -P4 -I{} runtune probe --trace={} --kernels=profile_set --dry-run
kevin: done
kevin: ```
jia: love the sampling approach. add decay to tenant historical estimates so we don't chase outdated profiles. something like: estimate = gamma * latest_sample + (1-gamma) * historic_estimate. gamma tuned per-tenant.
sam: eviction interaction: if we prioritize probes for a tenant, we must pin prefill KV cache for a short lease to benefit warmup. otherwise we probe, evict, probe again. propose lease = max(30s, 0.1 * median_inflight_request_latency).
olivia: on metrics, add `probe_effectiveness = tokens_served_with_new_kernel / probe_cost_tokens` and `probe_latency_delta`. ALARMS: if probe_effectiveness < 0.2 over 10m, auto-suspend probes for that tenant.
dmitri: rollout strategy: canary kernels for 1% traffic, then probe budget bump, measure `p99_latency` and `cost_per_token`. automatic rollback if p99 increases > 5% or cost_per_token increases > 10%.
maria: edge case: short-lived tenants (burst jobs) that never accumulate historic estimates. default to conservative kernels + opportunistic probes with strict cap. also think about multi-tenant fairness across dedicated pools vs shared pools.
kevin: ops note: need scheduler changes to enforce per-tenant probe tokens at node level. current probe accounting is global. i can stub an admission check in the scheduler: `if tenant_probe_tokens[node][tenant] + req.tokens > node_cap return reject`.
ops-bot: deploy: probe-token-enforcement patch deployed to canary pool at 2025-11-03T09:12Z (sha: a1b2c3).
jia: one more algorithm sketch (pseudocode):
jia: ```
jia: for each tenant:
jia:  score = sla_weight * norm_qps + expected_speedup_estimate
jia:  allocate = min(max_base, proportional_share(score))
jia:  if recent_probe_effectiveness < threshold: reduce allocate by factor r
jia: ```
dmitri: agree. let's collect 48h of probe_effectiveness per-tenant, then run an offline optimizer to fit alpha/beta/gamma and caps. we can run weekly scheduled re-tuning.
maria: ok action items: 1) kevin -> implement per-node probe caps (canary done by ops-bot), 2) olivia -> add probe consumption + effectiveness panels, 3) jia -> prototype sampling + decay code, 4) dmitri -> design canary rollback criteria and weekly optimizer. i'll file RFC follow-up PR with these items.
sam: also add a short doc on observable failure modes (probe storms, pin-and-evict loops). helps support triage. :memo:
maria: thanks everyone. i'll send the PR and link here. :thumbsup:
